## What pathways drive the ICR–FAO relationship in Basal tumors?

```{python}
import pandas as pd 
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
```

```{python}
de_results = pd.read_csv("de_results.csv", index_col = 0)
de_results.head()
```

## Create ranked gene list for GSEA

```{python}
mitopathways = pd.read_excel(
    "Human.MitoCarta3.0.xls",
    sheet_name="C MitoPathways"
)

print(mitopathways.columns.tolist())
```

```{python}
mitopathways = pd.read_excel(
    "Human.MitoCarta3.0.xls",
    sheet_name="C MitoPathways"
)
fao_genes = mitopathways.loc[
    mitopathways["MitoPathway"] == "Fatty acid oxidation","Genes"].dropna().tolist()
```

```{python}
fao_genes
```

```{python}
icr_genes = [
    "IFNG","TBX21","IL12B","STAT1","IRF1",
    "CD8A","CD8B",
    "CXCL9","CXCL10","CCL5",
    "GNLY","PRF1","GZMA","GZMB","GZMH",
    "CD274","PDCD1","CTLA4","IDO1","FOXP3",
]
genes_to_exclude = set(icr_genes) | set(fao_genes)
de_filtered = de_results.loc[~de_results.index.isin(genes_to_exclude)]
ranking = de_filtered["logFC"] * -np.log10(de_filtered["p"])
ranking = ranking.sort_values(ascending=False)
```

## Run GSEA

```{python}

import gseapy as gp


gsea_res = gp.prerank(
    rnk=ranking,
    gene_sets="MSigDB_Hallmark_2020", 
    outdir="gsea_basal_fao_normed",
    permutation_num=1000,
    seed=42,
    verbose=True
)
```

```{python}
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", None)

pd.set_option("display.width", None)
```

## Top significant pathways

```{python}
gsea_res.res2d.sort_values("FDR q-val").head(10)
```

```{python}
sig = gsea_res.res2d[gsea_res.res2d["FDR q-val"] < 0.05]

sig[["Term", "NES", "FDR q-val", "Lead_genes"]].head(15)
```

- **FAO-high Basal-like tumors (**immune-hot)**:** interferon/antigen-presentation, OXPHOS, adipogenesis, fatty acid metabolism - all up

- **FAO-low Basal-like tumors(**immune-cold)**:** EMT, hypoxia, glycolysis, angiogenesis, TGF-beta, NF-kB, proliferation markers - all up

- FAO-low tumors look more like classic aggressive, oxygen-starved, sugar-burning, invasive tumors; FAO-high tumors look more oxidative, calmer, and more visible to the immune system.

```{python}
def check_pathway_gene_overlap(gsea_res, genes_to_exclude) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    genes_to_exclude: the same set we built for the ranking step
                       (icr_genes | fao_genes), to confirm none of them
                       leaked into the significant pathway hits.
    """
    res2d = gsea_res.res2d.copy()
    rows = []
    for _, row in res2d.iterrows():
        leading_edge = set(row["Lead_genes"].split(";"))
        overlap = sorted(leading_edge & genes_to_exclude)
        rows.append({
            "Term": row["Term"],
            "NES": row["NES"],
            "FDR q-val": row["FDR q-val"],
            "n_leading_edge": len(leading_edge),
            "n_overlap_excluded": len(overlap),
            "overlapping_genes": ", ".join(overlap) if overlap else "-",
        })
    overlap_df = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("FDR q-val")

    if overlap_df["n_overlap_excluded"].sum() == 0:
        print("Clean: no leading-edge genes overlap with icr_genes/fao_genes.")
    else:
        print("Check flagged terms below — some leading-edge genes overlap excluded genes.")
    return overlap_df


overlap_check = check_pathway_gene_overlap(gsea_res, genes_to_exclude)
overlap_check.head(10)
```

no overlap
